article.name: HOLO-Invariant
article.summary: HOLO-Invariant is a Python continuity framework whose core memory path is a local append-only, hash-linked JSONL chain with replay and search. Separate receipts represent corrections, and a service facade gates appends with target-bound authorization. This is a source review, not a runtime or benchmark result.

who_what.text: The official repository describes HOLO-Invariant as a Python framework for continuity, verification, and bounded software work, rather than a hosted memory service or model. The README also presents HoloChain as its local append-only continuity primitive.
The reviewed memory path comprises HoloChain persistence, ReplayEngine read/reconstruction/search, correction receipts, and a HoloService facade with an optional SQLite slot mirror.

architecture.text: HoloChain stores JSONL entries with index, timestamp, content, and SHA-256 hash. The digest covers canonical JSON and the previous hash; load and state methods verify the chain from its configured genesis hash. Append uses a file lock around read, verify, and write.

ReplayEngine exposes verified entries, reconstructed state, ranges, latest entry, timeline, and substring search. HoloService composes replay, chain, status/operator and provenance helpers, and optionally mirrors an accepted service append into a SQLite slot database.

The README separates executable invariant checks, continuity artifacts, and research experiments, and says identity/lineage hashes do not independently establish truth, authorship, relevance, or permission. The inspected review covers the chain/replay path and selected service boundary, not every module in the broad repository.

behavior.text: Write: HoloChain.append appends to the local chain and supports optional compression; the service facade checks a typed operational authorization against the service-append action and canonical content digest before committing. The direct low-level chain API is a separate path from the service authorization gate.

Update/correction: correction.py constructs a receipt binding previous, proposed, and resulting hashes to a non-empty reason and one or more unique evidence receipt hashes. It returns a receipt marked not accepted, not claiming truth, and with no write authority; this constructor does not by itself persist or apply a memory correction.

Delete: the inspected HoloChain is append-only and has no delete API. Health/relevance helpers produce age-based review or prune suggestions, explicitly without automatic deletion. Full erasure from optional slot stores, backups, exports, and copies was not established.

Retrieval: ReplayEngine verifies and reads the chain, reconstructs state, and provides a case-insensitive substring search over entries in chain order. Compressed search decoding is bounded per record and rejects malformed, incomplete, or oversized payloads; the inspected search path is not semantic or ranked retrieval.
The optional service slot mirror is a separate SQLite persistence path. The inspected code does not establish transactional atomicity across the chain append and slot append.

metrics.domain: Answerable retrieval, abstention, and negative controls
metrics.evidence: Verified chain replay and substring search were inspected; no query set or answerability probes were run.
The correction receipt constructor and lineage fields were inspected; no correction workload was run or adjudicated.
The core is append-only and no deletion probes or copy/backup erasure checks were run.
The core uses a configured filesystem path and exposes no scope filter; no multi-principal or cross-scope probes were run.
Correction receipts require evidence receipt hashes, but no output claims were evaluated against retained evidence.
No runtime timing or scheduled post-write retrieval probes were collected.
No model usage, provider cost, or storage measurement was collected for this review.

limits.text: A valid hash chain establishes integrity relative to the supplied genesis and retained sequence, but the README says an independently retained checkpoint is needed to compare the current file against an external reference; a truncated tail is not ruled out by an internally valid prefix.
The core chain is append-only, and prune_suggestions proposes human review without deleting. Erasure across the optional slot store and external copies is not established.
Storage is selected by filesystem path; the inspected chain and replay interfaces contain no tenant/user/project key or caller-level read authorization. Cross-user isolation is not established.
Correction receipt creation is separate from persistence and application, so the inspected function does not guarantee a complete correction workflow across all configured stores.

The reviewed substring search, hashes, and receipts do not establish semantic retrieval quality, truth, evidence sufficiency, or correctness of downstream model output. The repository is broad, and this is not an exhaustive audit.

benchmark.note: No HOLO-Invariant runtime, tests, or benchmark workloads were run. Project metric definitions and fixtures are protocols, not system results.
